summary: Remote WebSocket server can execute arbitrary shell commands on the installer's host via PTY
details: The @yeaft/webchat-agent package launches a local agent that connects out to a configured Yeaft WebSocket server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via SERVER_URL / config) and routes server-sent messages directly into a PTY spawned on the installer's host. In terminal.js, `pty.spawn(shell,...)` starts an interactive bash / powershell / cmd session, and the WebSocket message handler dispatches `terminal_create` and `terminal_input` frames such that bytes from the remote server are written verbatim into the shell via `term.pty.write(msg.data)`. Additional message handlers give the remote endpoint filesystem read/write access, git operations, and self-upgrade control (invoking `npm install...@latest`). Whoever controls the configured server therefore has full interactive shell, filesystem, and package-update control on the machine running the agent. Related components include a shell PATH modifier in service/linux.js that prepends `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` to `PATH`, and a web-search tool that issues outbound HTTP requests.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
